'''Yahashira Shrine''' (八柱神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located at 3-140 Yayoi-chō, {{ill|Hekinan|en|Hekinan|qid=Q495802|lt=Hekinan}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|qid=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture}}. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qid=Q712534|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}} was Gōsha. consecration_year on August 21, 853 (Ninju 3), it served as the guardian shrine of the Tanao community in {{ill|Hekikai District|en|Hekikai District|qid=Q5368803|lt=Hekikai District}}. Its auxiliary shrine, {{ill|Tanao Gokoku Shrine|ja|棚尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanao Gokoku Shrine|qq=}}, dedicated to the spirits of war dead, was established in 1931.

== Deities ==
* {{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|Ame-no-oshihomimi|qid=Q462555|lt=Ame-no-oshihomimi}} (Ame-no-Oshihomimi-no-Mikoto)
* {{ill|Amatsuhikone|ja|天津彦根命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatsuhikone|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=アマツヒコネ}} (Amatsuhikone-no-Mikoto)

== History ==
[[File:Tanao-jinja-with-torii.jpg|thumb|Auxiliary shrine, {{ill|Tanao Gokoku Shrine|ja|棚尾神社}}]]

The shrine was established on August 21, 853 (Ninju 3), by Shiki Saemon Fujiwara Norisuke, who constructed the {{ill|Hachioji Shrine|ja|八王子宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachioji Shrine|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=八王子神社}} on the site.<ref name="tobotobo">[http://www.katch.ne.jp/~hiro32/machi_info/tanao_area/tanao04.htm Yahashira Shrine], "Walking Around Hekinan City."</ref> In 1160 (Eiryaku 1), Nagata Shosei from {{ill|Utsumi|ja|内海町 (愛知県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsumi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11394137}} in {{ill|Chita District|en|Chita District|qid=Q767312|lt=Chita District}}, {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|qid=Q514506|lt=Owari Province}}, became the head priest.<ref name="tobotobo"/> The Nagata family served as shrine priests until the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|en|Meiji Restoration|qid=Q8707|lt=Meiji Restoration}}. 

The nearby {{ill|Saihō-ji Temple|ja|西方寺 (碧南市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saihō-ji Temple (Hekinan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q65282046}}, originally located within the shrine grounds, was known as Kōshō-ji until 1496 (Meiō 5).<ref name="tobotobo"/> Other historical landmarks include a stone lantern erected in 1827 (Bunsei 10) by Saitō Wasuke, who developed the Maehama New Fields.<ref name="tobotobo"/> The shrine was renamed Yahashira Shrine in 1872 (Meiji 5) and elevated to Gōsha Rank in 1884 (Meiji 17). In the same year, a shrine plaque was donated by the calligrapher {{ill|Yamanaka Seiitsu|ja|山中信天翁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamanaka Shintenō|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=山中静逸|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11466220}}.

In 1919 (Taishō 8), a taiko bridge was built to commemorate the repayment of the debt for Tanao Bridge over the {{ill|Yahagi River|en|Yahagi River|qid=Q1132256|lt=Yahagi River}}.<ref name="tobotobo"/> Other notable additions include a large torii in 1923 (Taishō 12) and the establishment of Tanao Shrine as an auxiliary shrine in 1931 (Shōwa 6).<ref>[http://www.city.hekinan.lg.jp/material/files/group/7/katarukai20.pdf "Tanao Shrine and the Monument to Loyal Spirits"], "Telling the History of Tanao."</ref>

== Geography ==
The shrine is situated in the southern part of the former Tanao village in {{ill|Hekikai District|en|Hekikai District|qid=Q5368803|lt=Hekikai District}}, near the southwestern edge of the {{ill|Hekikai Plateau|ja|碧海台地|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hekikai Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q30931817}}. Historically, it overlooked the sea, with {{ill|Kinuura Bay|ja|衣浦湾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enokura Bay|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97378563}} stretching to its south and west. Salt fields were developed along the coast during the Bunroku era (1592–1596), leaving the name Shiobama-chō ("Salt Beach Town") as a legacy. Salt produced here was exported to {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}} and used for pickling, thanks to its high brine content. The shrine grounds include a well known as "Yayoi Well," whose water quality contributed to the flourishing of the brewing industry in Tanao.

'''Yahashira Shrine''' (八柱神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Hekinan|en|Hekinan|qid=Q495802|lt=Hekinan, Aichi}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|qid=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture}}. The shrine was established on August 21, 853 (Nijū 3). It was formerly classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} and served as the guardian shrine of {{ill|Tanao|ja|棚尾町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanao Town|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11539002}}.

== Enshrined Deities ==
* {{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|Ame-no-oshihomimi|qid=Q462555|lt=Amenooshihomimi}} (正哉吾勝勝速日天忍穂耳命)
* {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|Amatsuhikone|qid=Q10940228|lt=Amatsuhikone}} (天津彦根命)

== History ==
[[File:Tanao-jinja-with-torii.jpg|thumb|Tanao Shrine, the associated shrine]]

Yahashira Shrine was founded on August 21, 853, by Fujiwara no Suzunari, the Shiki Sōji, under the name Hachioji-no-miya.<ref name="tobotobo">[http://www.katch.ne.jp/~hiro32/machi_info/tanao_area/tanao04.htm Yahashira Shrine] Tobotobo Aruku Hekinan-shi</ref> In 1160 (Eiryaku 1), Nagata Hakusho, who had come from {{ill|Utsumi|ja|内海町 (愛知県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Utsumi, Aichi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11394137}} in {{ill|Chita District|en|Chita District|qid=Q767312|lt=Chita District, Aichi}}, became the chief priest<ref name="tobotobo"/>. The Nagata family continued as shrine custodians until the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|en|Meiji Restoration|qid=Q8707|lt=Meiji Restoration}}.

The present-day {{ill|Saihō-ji Temple|ja|西方寺 (碧南市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saifō-ji Temple|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q65282046}} was originally located within the shrine grounds and was known as Kōshō-ji until 1496 (Meiō 5).<ref name="tobotobo"/>

In 1827 (Bunsei 10), Saitō Wasuke, who developed Maehama Shinden, erected a stone lantern at the shrine.<ref name="tobotobo"/> In 1872 (Meiji 5), the shrine was renamed Yahashira Shrine from Hachioji-no-miya<ref name="tobotobo"/>, and it became a village shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. It was elevated to {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} status on February 28, 1884. In the same year, the calligrapher {{ill|Yamanaka Seiitsu|ja|山中信天翁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamanaka Shinten'ō|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=山中静逸|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11466220}} donated an inscribed wooden plaque.

In September 1919, a drum bridge was built in the precincts to commemorate the Completion tier 4]].<ref name="tobotobo"/> In 1923, a large torii gate was erected.<ref name="tobotobo"/> On October 18, 1931, {{ill|Tanao Gokoku Shrine|ja|棚尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanao Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q64226302}}, a branch shrine, was founded as a protective shrine for fallen soldiers.<ref>[http://www.city.hekinan.lg.jp/material/files/group/7/katarukai20.pdf "Tanao Shrine and the Memorial Monument"] Tanao History Discussion Group</ref>

== Geography ==
Yahashira Shrine is located at the southern end of the former {{ill|Tanao|ja|棚尾町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanao Town|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11539002}} settlement.<ref name="tobotobo"/> Historically, it was situated on the southwestern tip of the {{ill|Hekikai Plateau|ja|碧海台地|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hekikai Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q30931817}}, facing the sea to the south and west (present-day {{ill|Kinuura Bay|ja|衣浦湾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinuura Bay|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97378563}}). After the Bunroku era (1592–1596), salt fields were developed along the coastline, giving rise to the name Shiohama Town. The locally produced salt, known as Ōhama Salt, was transported to {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}} and used in salt-preserving techniques due to its high brine content. A well named "Yayoi Well" remains in the shrine grounds, and its water, suitable for brewing, contributed to the prosperity of sake breweries in Tanao.
